rounds.text: Compounded profit growth stands at an exceptional 46% over 5 years and 52% over 3 years, demonstrating outstanding fundamental acceleration that comfortably outpaces the 35% compounded share price growth over the same 5-year span [E19, E20, E23]. Return metrics are exceptionally strong across the board, with ROE at 26.0%, ROCE at 25.5%, and a 10-year median ROE of 17% that scales up to 26% over the last year [E12, E13, E26, E29]. Valuation appears highly attractive as the stock trades at a P/E of 16.1x compared to a sector benchmark of 21.41x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 10.05x versus its sector benchmark of 12.12x [E1, E6, E11]. Institutional confidence is surging with positive money flow as foreign and domestic institutions increased their holdings by 1.51 and 5.37 percentage points respectively since December 2023, while operating margins expanded by 7 percentage points over three years to reach 22% in the TTM [E30, E42, E43, E44]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that today's market price of ₹ 505 implies a mere 5.2% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0%, offering a substantial disconnect between current pricing and actual operational delivery [E2, E47]. Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.27x for March 2026 with negative free cash flow of ₹ -19 Cr, and borrowings have increased to ₹ 101 Cr alongside potential interest capitalization [E34, E36, E39, E58].

A severe disconnect plagues Dhabriya Polywood Ltd, where reported profits completely fail to translate into actual liquidity, as evidenced by a dreadful cash conversion ratio of just 0.27x for March 2026 [E34]. This divergence leaves the company bleeding cash with a deeply negative free cash flow of Rs -19 Cr in March 2026 [E36], while total borrowings ballooned to Rs 101 Cr by September 2026 compared to Rs 76 Cr a year prior [E39]. Compounding these aggressive debt-funded capital expenditures, official filings explicitly flag the real risk that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E58]. Meanwhile, the stock offers a total dividend yield of 0.00%, offering zero cash return to shareholders despite the touted earnings [E4]. Valuation multiples also reflect hidden vulnerability, as the price-to-book ratio of 3.64x trades at a sharp premium against the sector benchmark of 2.4x [E7]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong profit growth of 46.2% CAGR over the last 5 years [E57].

Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.27x [E34], free cash flow is negative at Rs -19 Cr [E35, E36], borrowings rose to Rs 101 Cr [E39], the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], and official filings flag a risk of interest capitalization [E58]. However, the bear's focus on rising borrowings ignores that this debt fuels a strategic capex build-up, with CWIP surging by 50.0% to Rs 9 Cr [E40] under a supportive Capital Goods sector tailwind of +0.58 [E67]. While the P/B ratio trades at a premium to the sector benchmark [E7], this is fully justified by superior operational metrics, including an ROE of 23.06% versus the sector's 11.11% [E9], an ROCE of 20.83% against 12.96% [E10], and an EV/EBITDA of 10.05x that undercuts the sector benchmark of 12.12x [E11]. Furthermore, the market price of Rs 505 implies an earnings growth expectation of only 5.2%, creating a massive disconnect from the 18.0% base-case assumption and offering a substantial 60.5% margin of safety [E2, E47, E46]. Fundamentals continue to outpace the stock price with a robust 46% profit growth over 5 years [E54, E57], while institutional money flow remains distinctly positive with a holding change of +5.55 percentage points [E44].

Conceded: the Capital Goods sector tailwind score is +0.58 [E67] and institutional money flow shows a holding increase of +5.55 percentage points [E44]. However, dismissing rising borrowings misses that total debt expanded to Rs 101 Cr while cash conversion collapsed to a dismal 0.27x and free cash flow plummeted to negative Rs 19 Cr [E34, E36, E39]. Conceded: the EV/EBITDA is 10.05x [E11], but referencing a sector comparison ignores that the price-to-book ratio sits at an elevated 3.64x against a sector benchmark of just 2.4x [E7]. Furthermore, pointing to a capital-intensive CWIP build-up of Rs 9 Cr that surged 50.0% validates the fundamental concern that the company might be capitalizing interest costs rather than generating real liquidity [E40, E58]. Finally, the screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating, undermining the reliability of any projected growth gap or margin of safety [E64].
